   City Council Staff Report

  DATE: February 21, 2024
  AGENDA ITEM NO: Consent Calendar - 3C

 TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
 FROM:  Martha Garcia, Director of Finance
 SUBJECT:  Direct the City Manager to implement the approved water rates effective
  March 1, 2024

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Directing the City Manager to implement the approved water rates effective
  March 1, 2024; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
Ordinance No. 2239 became effective January 19, 2024. It increases water rates by the
following percentages: year 1, 32%; year 2, 8%; year 3, 8%; year 4, 7%; and year 5, 8%.
These rates were scheduled to increase beginning February 1, 2024.

During the November 15, 2023 City Council meeting, Council directed the City Manager
to explore bond financing in order to provide an upfront infusion of funding for water
infrastructure needs. Since then, the City Manager and Finance Director have worked
with a team of experts on bond financing. This process has taken longer than originally
anticipated due to challenges in collecting historical data for the bond disclosure and loan
documents. On January 17, the City Council postponed implementing the increased water
rates until after the City Council considers issuing bonds for infrastructure financing.

On February 7, the City Council received a status report regarding the challenges still
being encountered in the bond process. As explained below, the City Manager and
Finance Director recommend that the City Council approve implementation of lower water
rates starting March 1, 2024.

BACKGROUND:
Ordinance No. 2239 increased water rates that the maximum percentages outlined
above. The City Council also considered the utility rate study prepared by HF&H that
suggests water rates may be lowered if the City issues water infrastructure bonds.

Specifically, HF&H proposes that the City may reduce the rate increases as follows
(based upon years 1-5): 26%, 8%, 8%, 7%. 7%. This rate structure was expected to
generate $32.6 million for the period beginning January 1, 2024, through FY 2027-28.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Receiving and Filing the Notice of Completion for CIP 99025 – Monterey Pass
  Road Waterline Improvements, recorded by the Public Works Director on February
  5, 2024;
  2. Adopting a resolution terminating the local emergency governing the Monterey
  Pass Road Waterline Project; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
On August 17, 2022, City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R69 authorizing the City
Manager to take necessary measures for emergency repair of a water main line on
Monterey Pass Road. The City added the Monterey Pass Road Waterline Improvements
to the City’s Capital Improvement Program (“CIP”) as Project No. 99025. The project is
now complete, and it is recommended that the City Council receive and file the Notice of
Completion and adopt a resolution terminating the local emergency governing the
Monterey Pass Road Waterline Project.

BACKGROUND:
Pursuant to Resolution No. 2022-R69, the City Manager exercised emergency powers to
complete the Monterey Pass Road Waterline Improvements project. Recurring water
main leaks in several areas within Monterey Pass Road between the intersections of
Vagabond Drive and Brightwood Street resulted in extensive infrastructure damage to the
roadway and necessary water main pipe repairs to ensure continued water service to
residences and businesses in the area.

As a result, the City took immediate action required by that emergency, to procure the
necessary equipment, services, and supplies to complete required improvements, without
giving notice for bids to let contracts. The design phase was completed in December
2022. Construction started in March 2023 with major construction work completed in
December of 2023. Minor items such as red curb painting was completed in January
2024.

The construction part of the project is now 100% complete. On February 5, 2024, the
Public Works directors completed the Notice of Completion in accordance with
Resolution No. 11701.

The contractor completed the installation of the 12-inch pipeline for the entire project from
Floral Drive to Vagabond Road for a total length of 10,800 linear feet of pipeline. This is
the backbone of the water distribution system along Monterey Pass Road. The contractor
also completed the installation of all interconnecting pipes including the connection at
Vagabond Road, lateral pipelines for the water services, fire services, and fire hydrants
for the project. Additionally, the contractor completed hydrostatic pressure testing of the
pipeline.

The project resulted in the following installations:
  - 10,740 linear feet of 12-inch main pipeline
  - 24 fire hydrants
  - 3 main interconnecting pipes
  - 69 new water services
  - 21 fire service lines
  - 4 storm drain pipes

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
On September 6, 2023 the Public Works Director solicited proposals for a fleet and fuel
management software system that provides vehicle tracking, maintenance scheduling,
inventory management, fuel distribution management, and real-time reporting of these
activities for the City’s fleet division. Two bids were received in response to the request
for proposals. The Public Works Director completed his review of bids, and
recommends that City Council award a contract to Faster Asset Solutions, the
lowest responsible bidder, in the amount of $508,202.00, for a five year term.

BACKGROUND
In 2022, the City with assistance from Eide Bailly Consultants, completed an assessment
of the City’s Fleet division. The final report resulted in various improvement
recommendations, including the procurement of an updated fuel and fleet management
system. Such a system would manage all vehicular and designated equipment type
assets owned, maintained, and operated by the City.

On September 6, 2023, the City posted notice inviting formal bids at City Hall and on the
City’s website for a fleet and fuel management software system. The proposed system is
a web-based management solution that provides vehicle tracking, maintenance
scheduling, inventory management, fuel distribution management, and real-time reporting
of these activities. The notice inviting bids also requires the vendor to provide software,
hardware, training, and technical support to ensure the successful implementation and
continued use of the software system and all related components.

The deadline for submitting bids was September 28, 2023. On this date, two bids were
opened by the City Clerk’s office:

 SUBJECT:  Planning services augmentation with Willdan Group, Inc.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Authorizing the City Manager to utilize Willdan Group, Inc. for providing routine
  planning services to assist the Community Development Department, not to
  exceed $150,000 annually; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
On January 26, 2024, the City executed an on-call professional services agreement with
the Willdan Group to provide special planning services for tasks associated with
processing the Atlantic Square land use applications. TRC is the applicant for these
applications and is reimbursing the City for all of Willdan’s services.

The Community Development Director would like to supplement the City’s routine
planning services with Willdan’s assistance. This need is a result of the City’s ongoing
struggle in finding qualified employees to fully staff the City’s various departments.

Willdan’s professional services agreement allows the City to issue task orders for various
services. Here, the requested action is to authorize the City Manager to issue a task order
for supplemental planning services in an amount not to exceed $150,000 per year.

BACKGROUND:
The City selected Willdan Group to assist with processing various land use applications
including (initially) TRC’s proposals for the Atlantic Square development. Willdan Group’s
agreement with the City also allows it to perform additional, separate, planning and design
professional services for the City.

As the City Council is aware, all employers are challenged by finding qualified individuals
to fill employment vacancies. Here, the Community Development Director advised the
City Manager that critical planning tasks are being delayed because of staffing shortages.

Willdan Group can help facilitate the prompt processing of routine planning needs. These
include, drafting new zoning regulations needed to implement the General Plan including

  Page 451 of 576
 the Housing Element; processing ministerial projects; architectural review; landscape
review; assistance with public inquires; project management for review of land use and
development applications including residential (e.g., single family, multi-family residential,
and accessory dwelling units), commercial, and mixed-use development projects;
environmental review; report and letter writing; and presentations and attendance at
public hearings, as necessary.

2023-2024 STRATEGIC PLAN GOAL:
This contract with services to provide staff augmentation meets the goals of housing and
economic development by streamlining and expediting the processing of projects that
can include both housing and commercial development that will increase housing stock
and provide economic opportunities for businesses within the City.

FISCAL IMPACT:

savings resulting from on-going vacancies in the Community Development Department
and from developer deposit fees. No additional funding is being requested for this task

RECOMMENDATION:

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
Adoption of this Resolution is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(“CEQA”) under CEQA Guidelines § 15061(b)(3) 15061 because it can be seen with
certainty that there is no possibility that the Resolution may have a significant effect on
the environment.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The County of Los Angeles Department of Agriculture Commissioner/Weights and
Measures (Weed Abatement Division) has submitted the annual Weed Abatement
Declaration List to the City. The Weed Abatement Declaration List (“Declaration List”) is
a list of parcels in Monterey Park which have been identified by inspection to contain, or
have the potential to contain weeds, brush or other flammable materials sufficient to be
considered a fire hazard. The accompanying Resolution seeks City Council approval to
declare the properties on the annual Weed Abatement Declaration List to be public
nuisances which may be abated. The authority to remove properties from the Declaration
List, upon request and after investigation, will be assigned to the City Manager or
designee.

BACKGROUND:
In 1992, the City of Monterey Park entered into a contract with the Los Angeles County
Department of Agriculture Commissioner/Weights and Measures (“County”) to provide
weed abatement services to the City. At that time, both the Fire and Community
Development Departments worked in unison to address and abate the weeds in the
community. Subsequent to reviewing the County’s proposal, the City determined that the
County could better provide the weed abatement services currently handled by the City,
thereby realizing a significant savings in staff time and financial resources. Moreover, the
contract with the County would also free up Fire and Code Enforcement staff, allowing
time to focus on other important issues in the community. Since 1992, the County Weed

Abatement program assisted in a reduction of fire calls for service for vegetation-related
fires.

The annual weed abatement process is a way to remind property owners of their
responsibility to maintain their properties to minimize fire hazards in the community. The
Weed Abatement cycle begins with a City-wide inspection of private properties,
conducted by the County; based on this inspection, the County compiles a Weed
Abatement Declaration List (“Declaration List”) which identifies properties in the City that
contain, or have the potential to contain, weeds or brush sufficient to be considered a
public nuisance. The County has advised that it considers a parcel to be a future or
potential hazard if it is not completely landscaped or irrigated and there is a potential for
weed growth. The Monterey Park Fire Department then reviews the Declaration List by
independently conducting field inspections of the listed properties and either confirms or
rejects their placement the Declaration List. Once the properties on the Declaration List
have been confirmed by the City, the County mails notices to the recorded owner of each
parcel informing them that their parcel is an existing, future or "potential" hazard.

Property owners may voluntarily abate the nuisance conditions identified in the notice
issued by the County or appeal to the City Council to have their property removed from
the Declaration List. Following the appeals/voluntary abatement deadlines, any properties
identified in the Declaration List which remain out of compliance will be abated by the
County, the cost of which (including any re-inspection fees) will be imposed as a special
assessment against the property.

2024 WEED ABATEMENT CYCLE
The County submitted the 2024 Declaration List to the Fire Department; this list has
verified by the Fire Chief and Fire Marshal. The Declaration List presently before the
Council identifies a total of 1,610 improved and unimproved parcels for this year. The
County mailed notices on or about January 4, 2024 to the recorded owner of each parcel
included on the Declaration List. The County advised that this year's Declaration List
includes parcels that continue to lack landscaping/irrigation as well as new parcels
identified via complaints submitted by residents, new inspections, and field surveys by
County inspectors. Lastly, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors established an
inspection fee of $51.59 for the 2024 abatement cycle. This inspection fee is a $3.50
increase from last year's fee and will be assessed against all parcels identified on the
Declaration List, regardless of whether the County is required to clear the parcel by the
stated deadline date.

 TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
 FROM:  Scott Wiese, Chief of Police
 SUBJECT:  Consideration and possible action to adopt a Resolution amending the
  Monterey Park Bail Schedule and requesting the presiding judge of the Los
  Angeles Superior Court approve the amended bail schedule for
  misdemeanor and infraction violations of the Monterey Park Municipal Code

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopting a Resolution amending the Monterey Park Bail Schedule and requesting the
  presiding judge of the Los Angeles Superior Court approve the amended bail schedule
  for misdemeanor and infraction violations of the Monterey Park Municipal Code;
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
In May 2021, the City Council adopted a bail schedule which the Los Angeles Superior Court
Executive Committee approved for use on September 15, 2021 (the “Bail Schedule”). The
Bail Schedule was adopted to allow the City the opportunity to address Monterey Park
Municipal Code (“MPMC”) violations that affect the quality of life in the City and a result of
Los Angeles District Attorney George Gascon’s non-prosecution policy for a range of
misdemeanor offenses. Since the Bail Schedule’s adoption, the City has adopted new
regulations that are not reflected in the Bail Schedule and, therefore, that cannot be
prosecuted. Accordingly, it is recommended that the City Council adopt the attached
Resolution amending the Bail Schedule and granting the City Manager authority to amend
the Bail Schedule from time to time to ensure that MPMC violations can be prosecuted.

BACKGROUND AND DISCUSSION:
A bail schedule establishes the amount a person booked into jail must post for release as
security to ensure their appearance at a future court date. Additionally, for the Court to accept
misdemeanor or infraction violations of the MPMC for criminal prosecution, a bail amount
must be established for each MPMC section the City wishes the court to hear.

In December 2020, Los Angeles County District Attorney George Gascon (“DA”) announced
he would no longer prosecute a range of “low level” misdemeanor offenses. This includes
quality-of-life crimes, such as trespass, disturbing the peace, criminal threats, resisting arrest,
loitering, and public intoxication. The DA’s non-prosecution directives also apply to any
violation “falling within the spirit” of this policy, which necessarily includes violations of the
MPMC.

Since, December 2020, the Police Chief has referred select criminal cases that substantially
impact the quality of life in the City to the DA for prosecution, only to have the DA reject the
case and invoice the City for the DA’s time in reviewing and rejecting the cases. While not all
cases will rise to the level of prosecution, amending the Bail Schedule is necessary to ensure
that crimes which have a serious impact on residents’ quality of life can be and are
prosecuted.

On January 21, 2023, 11 people were murdered and 9 were severely injured as a result of a
shooting spree by an individual using a modified firearm during the Lunar New Year
celebration. In response to the shooting, the City Council adopted, among other things,
firearms regulations including safe firearm storage within residences, prohibiting firearms on
public property, and creating a health protection zone.

The proposed Resolution amends the Bail Schedule by including regulations that were
adopted after the Bail Schedule was approved, including the aforementioned firearm
regulations, regulations that were inadvertently omitted when the Bail Schedule was
approved, and would grant the City Manager the authority to periodically amend the Bail
Schedule to include newly adopted regulations.

FISCAL IMPACT:
Adopting the Resolution itself will have a nominal fiscal impact in requiring the Assistant City
Attorney or Deputy City Attorney to appear in court up to one day per month to prosecute
misdemeanor MPMC violations. The City will receive offsetting revenue from fines paid by
persons prosecuted. It is difficult to predict exactly how much the City will receive from such
fines.

  authority to establish bails for violations within a county lies exclusively with the courts.
  California law provides for the approval by the Superior Court of a schedule of bails for
  those offenses for which bail may be posted and forfeited;

  Monterey Park Bail Schedule (“Bail Schedule”).

  approved the Bail Schedule.

  D. Since the Superior Court approved the Bail Schedule, the City has adopted ordinances
  amending the Monterey Park Municipal Code (“MPMC”), including, without limitation,
  firearm buffer zones and safe firearm storage.

  E. The City Council desires to amend the Bail Schedule to include MPMC offenses that
  were not previously included, thereby enabling the Los Angeles Superior Court to
  accept new violations of the MPMC for prosecution and to accurately process citations
  in accordance with the MPMC.

  Attorney, the Monterey Park Police Department Chief, and other staff members in the

  APPROVE THE ATTACHED BAIL SCHEDULE FOR MISDEMEANOR

  MUNICIPAL CODE

  The City Council of the City of Monterey Park does resolve as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds and declares that:

  A.  The City is statutorily authorized to establish fines for violations of municipal
  ordinances. That power does not extend to establishing bails for those
  violations. The authority to establish bails for violations within a county lies
  exclusively with the courts. California law provides for the approval by the
  Superior Court of a schedule of bails for those offenses for which bail may
  be posted and forfeited;

  B.  The City does not have a current bail schedule submitted to the Superior
  Court. In order for the Court to accept misdemeanor or infraction violations
  of the Monterey Park Municipal Code (“MPMC”) for criminal prosecution, a
  bail amount must be established for each MPMC section. Further, the
  Superior Court will use the bail schedule as a guide for imposing fine
  amounts when a violator is found guilty;

  C.  The Bail Schedule has been reviewed by the City Manager, the City
  Attorney, the Monterey Park Police Department, and other staff members
  in the areas which involve violations within their supervision or jurisdiction;
  and

  D.  The City Council desires to establish the City’s Bail Schedule to enable the
  Alhambra and Pasadena Courthouses to accept violations of the MPMC for
  prosecution and to accurately process citations in accordance with the
  MPMC.

SECTION 2: The City Council adopts the Monterey Park Bail Schedule attached as
Exhibit “A,” and incorporated by reference.

SECTION 3: The City Council requests that the Superior Court of the County of Los
Angeles approve the attached recommended Bail Schedule for violations of the Monterey
Park Municipal Code, attached as Exhibit “A.”

SECTION 4: The City Council authorizes the City Manager to make technical
amendments to the Bail Schedule, in a form approved by the City Attorney, when
desirable.

 SUBJECT:  Renewal of the County of Los Angeles General Services Agreement

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute a General Services Agreement with the
  County of Los Angeles in a form approved by the City Attorney; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
On March 6, 2019, the then-City Council authorized the renewal of the General Services
Agreement (GSA) with the County of Los Angeles (County) to provide certain services for
the City. The term of that agreement was from July 1, 2019, to June 30, 2024. To ensure
the continuation of the services, the City would need to renew a new five-year agreement.

BACKGROUND:
The County provides certain services to the City that have been agreed upon by the
County department providing the service. The actual services provided under the GSA
generally consist of miscellaneous services, which are requested from the County on an
as-needed basis. These services may include predatory animal control, direct
assessment collection, and a variety of public works activities. A listing of services
provided under the Fiscal Year 2024-2029 GSA is contained in the contract services
matrix, which has been incorporated by reference and designated as Attachment 2.

The agreement with the City of Monterey Park will terminate on June 30, 2024. ln order
for the County to continue to provide these services, the agreement will need to be
renewed and the new five-year term will be from July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2029.

FISCAL IMPACT:
The rates for the County services are adjusted annually by the LA County Auditor-
Controller in accordance with the policies and procedures for determining those rates as
adopted by the Board of Supervisors. County departments providing ongoing and specific
services of a varied and/or complex nature, such as law enforcement, public health code
enforcement, and animal care and control utilize Specific Services Agreements which are
handled directly by the individual service departments and contain the scope and details

  The City of Los Angeles contracts with the Departments of Beaches & Harbors and Fire for maintenance and lifeguard services for four beaches located within the city through a Joint Powers Agreement (JPA) with the County.

  The Fire Department provides beach lifeguard services to the City of El Segundo through a contract with Chevron.

  The Internal Services Department (ISD) provides IT services (mainframe access) for the City of Los Angeles and the City of Long Beach. ISD Fleet
section provides fuel to San Bernardino County's Public Works department and the City of La Puente for the LASD Sheriff Station. ISD provides Mail Services to the City Halls of the City of Los Angeles and the City of Long Beach. The ISD Operations Support unit rebuilt a vertical split case pump for the City of Glendale's Water and Power. The
ISD Power Plant provides chilled water for the A/C unit and heat for the Santa Clarita Library. ISD also provides the Santa Clarita Library testing for the irrigation backflow.

8

9
  The Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk provides Document Transfer Tax Collection services to 88 cities in the County. It also provides election services to all cities through an approved City Council resolution and adopted by the Board of Supervisors.
10
  The Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk's Your Online Document Archive (YODA) is in-house electronic archive system.

  The Data Information Management System (DIMS) is a contracted-system that manages voter registration information.

   RESOLUTION NO.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY
  PARK, AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE THE GENERAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK
  AND THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City of Monterey Park desires to renew its General Serves Agreement
with the County of Los Angeles and authorizes the Mayor to execute the same on behalf
of the City of Monterey Park.

SECTION 2: This Resolution will become effective immediately upon adoption and will
remain effective unless repealed or suspended.

SECTION 3: The City Clerk will certify to the passage and adoption of this Resolution;
will enter the same in the book of original Resolutions of said City; furnish a certified copy
to the County of Los Angeles; and will make a minute of the passage and adoption thereof
in the record of proceedings of the Council of said City, in the minutes of the meeting at

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The City of Monterey Park Fire Department received Notice of Funding Opportunity
(NOFO) from the Federal Management Agency (FEMA) regarding a formal invitation to
submit a full application for consideration of Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) funds.
The Fire Department (Department) seeks to submit two separate applications for this
grant funding cycle.

The first application is to replace the Department’s aging self-contained breathing
apparatus. If the City is awarded grant funds for this project, the total proposed budget is
$768,683.29, which includes a federal share request of $698,802.99, and a required
applicant match of $69,880.30. The application Activity Title is Personal Protective
Equipment: Respirator Decontamination System (SCBA).

The second application is to update the air compressor system at Fire Station 61. If the
City is awarded grant funds for this project, the total proposed budget is $99,511.72, which
includes a federal share request of $90,465.20, and a required applicant match of
$9,046.52. The application Activity Title is Personal Protective Equipment: Air
Compressor/Fill Station/Cascade System Replacement.

Staff asks that Council adopts a resolution authorizing the City Manager or designee, to
apply for, receive, and appropriate grant funds for the Fiscal Year 2023 Assistance to
Firefighters Grant Program for these two projects. The application is due March 8, 2024.

BACKGROUND:

Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus Application
The Assistance to Firefighters Grant (AFG) was established under FEMA in 2001 as a
funding resource for firefighters and first responders to obtain the necessary tools,
equipment, and other critical resources needed to safely perform job duties while
protecting the public.

In the first grant application, the Department seeks funding to replace the aging self-
contained breathing apparatuses (SCBAs). The SCBAs are a vital component to
firefighters as they are used to supply oxygen when responding to fire related incidents
and are considered critical Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). The certification for the
Department’s current SCBAs will expire in the next two to three years; they are no longer
being produced, making finding replacement parts nearly impossible. The desired new
SCBAs meets current and future National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) and
National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) standards. The new
SCBAs are lighter in weight and have newer technology, such as built in radio
communications and thermal imaging cameras, which significantly improve firefighter
safety and health.

If the City of Monterey Park is awarded grant funds for the replacement of the SCBAs,
the total proposed budget is $768,683.29, which includes a federal share request of
$698,802.99 and a required applicant match of $69,880.30. Per AFG, the required
applicant match is factored in accordance with the size of the applicant’s jurisdiction. For
jurisdictions with a population of 20,000 but less than 1,000,000, a ten percent match is
required.

Compressor Application
In the second grant application, the Department seeks funding to update the air
compressor system (system) in Fire Station 61. The system is used by the firefighters to
fill their self-contained breathing apparatuses (SCBAs) with oxygen. The SCBAs are used
to supply oxygen to firefighters responding to fire related incidents and are considered
critical Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). The SCBAs will expire in the forthcoming
years. The current air compressor will be inoperable with the new equipment. The system
is over 20 years old and cannot be retrofitted to comply with new industry standards. In
anticipation of new SCBAs, staff seeks to replace the legacy system with an upgraded air
compressor system.

If the City of Monterey Park is offered a grant award, the total proposed budget is
$99,511.72, which includes a federal share request of $90,465.20 and a required
applicant match of $9,046.52. Per AFG, the required applicant match is factored in

  RESOLUTION NO.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY
  PARK, CALIFORNIA, DECLARING AND RECOGNIZING MARCH 2-6,
  2024, AS READ ACROSS AMERICA WEEK

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A. The act of reading has been around for thousands of years since the invention of
  the written word, and in the earliest years, reading was a skill that only the wealthy
  and educated segment of society possessed. As the years progressed, more
  individuals began to read and write, and reading came to be the common skill that
  it is today.

  B. In 1998, the National Education Association (NEA) established the nation’s largest
  year-round celebration of reading known as NEA’s Read Across America which
  focuses on motivating children and teens to read through events, partnerships, and
  reading resources that are about everyone, for everyone.

  C. NEA’s Read Across America Day is celebrated every March 2 and commences
  Read Across America Week which spans through March 6. Read Across America
  Week is a celebration of reading and promotes adult involvement in the education
  of students throughout the nation.

  D. Across the nation, teachers, librarians, politicians, actors, athletes, parents,
  grandparents, and others develop Read Across America activities to bring reading
  excitement to children of all ages. Governors, mayors, and other elected officials
  recognize the role reading plays in their communities with proclamations and floor
  statements.

  E. The annual theme for NEA’s Read Across America Day and Week is to Create &
  Celebrate a Nation of Diverse Readers. Monterey Park Residents are encouraged
  to read books with children and promote NEA’s message that there is always room
  in the community for all readers.

  F. The City Council of the City of Monterey Park is committed to inspiring all residents,
  especially children and youth, to explore diverse perspectives and cultures through
  the eyes of others. Books provide lessons that improve the overall quality of life,
  encourage curiosity, promote knowledge, and support the countless possibilities
  available to every person.

  G. The Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library supports the NEA’s mission by providing
  access to diverse books for readers of all ages and encouraging caregivers to read
  with their children to help them discover their own voices and learn from the voices
  of others.

  Page 575 of 576
   H. The City Council of the City of Monterey Park encourages all residents to visit the
  Bruggemeyer Library and to stand firmly committed to promoting reading as the
  catalyst for students’ future academic success, their preparation for jobs of the
  future, and their ability to compete in a global economy, and hereby proclaim
  March 2-6, 2024, as Read Across America Week.

SECTION 2: Electronic Signatures. This Resolution may be executed with electronic
signatures in accordance with Government Code §16.5. Such electronic signatures will
be treated in all respects as having the same effect as an original signature.

SECTION 3: Recordation. The Mayor, or presiding officer, is authorized to sign this
Resolution, signifying its adoption by the City Council of the City of Monterey Park, and
the City Clerk, or her duly appointed deputy, may attest thereto.

SECTION 4: Effective Date. This Resolution will become effective immediately upon
adoption and will remain effective unless repealed or superseded.

  Ordinance No. 2239 became effective January 19, 2024. It increases water rates
  by the following percentages: year 1, 32%; year 2, 8%; year 3, 8%; year 4, 7%;
  and year 5, 8%. These rates were scheduled to increase beginning February 1,
  2024.

  During the November 15, 2023 City Council meeting, Council directed the City
  Manager to explore bond financing in order to provide an upfront infusion of
  funding for water infrastructure needs. Since then, the City Manager and Finance
  Director have worked with a team of experts on bond financing.

  The City of Monterey Park Fire Department received Notice of Funding Opportunity

  Grant (AFG) funds. The Fire Department (Department) seeks to submit two

  apparatus. If the City is awarded grant funds for this project, the total proposed

  and a required applicant match of $69,880.30. The application Activity Title is
  Personal Protective Equipment: Respirator Decontamination System (SCBA).

  If the City is awarded grant funds for this project, the total proposed budget is
  $99,511.72, which includes a federal share request of $90,465.20, and a required
  applicant match of $9,046.52. The application Activity Title is Personal Protective
  Equipment: Air Compressor/Fill Station/Cascade System Replacement.
